boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe outdoor and campus activities with no admission or purchase required.

cards.title: Walk the Lakeside Loop
cards.subtitle: Keystone State Park, near Latrobe
cards.notes: Meet at the trailhead and take the flat, ADA-accessible loop around Keystone Lake; pause together at the causeway or dam viewpoints.
cards.short_summary: A two-mile lakeside loop with accessible terrain and wildlife-viewing opportunities.
cards.evidence_claim: Keystone State Park’s Lakeside Loop is a 2.0-mile easiest-rated loop open for hiking and biking, with restrooms, water, and picnic tables at the trailhead.
cards.access_notes: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; follow posted park rules and trail conditions.

cards.title: Loop Davis Run Trail
cards.subtitle: Keystone State Park, near Latrobe
cards.notes: Choose the 1.25-mile Davis Run loop for a walking conversation through wetlands and upland forest; bring water and stay on marked paths.
cards.short_summary: A more-difficult loop that moves from wetlands into mixed forest.
cards.evidence_claim: Davis Run Trail is a 1.25-mile, more-difficult hiking loop at Keystone State Park and passes wetlands and upland forest.
cards.access_notes: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; use the marked hiking route.

cards.title: Hike McCune Run Trail
cards.subtitle: Keystone State Park, near Latrobe
cards.notes: Make a small-group plan for the 1.8-mile McCune Run loop, then connect only where trail signs and your route plan allow.
cards.short_summary: A 1.8-mile wooded loop that links with other Keystone trails.
cards.evidence_claim: McCune Run Trail is a 1.8-mile, more-difficult hiking loop at Keystone State Park that connects with Strawcutter and Davis Run trails.
cards.access_notes: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; stay on marked trails and use daylight hours.

cards.title: Take the Pine Trail
cards.subtitle: Keystone State Park, near Latrobe
cards.notes: Use this short connector for a low-commitment outdoor reset, stopping to look for birds and butterflies without leaving the trail corridor.
cards.short_summary: A brief pine-plantation connector suited to an easy outdoor break.
cards.evidence_claim: Pine Trail is a 0.3-mile easiest-rated connector trail at Keystone State Park; the page notes views of farm fields and large chestnut oaks.
cards.access_notes: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; wear appropriate shoes for natural-surface trails.

cards.title: Climb Stone Lodge Trail
cards.subtitle: Keystone State Park, near Latrobe
cards.notes: Gather a prepared group for this steeper loop from the visitor-center parking area; allow time to return well before dark.
cards.short_summary: A challenging forest loop with remnants of a springhouse and homestead.
cards.evidence_claim: Stone Lodge Trail is a 1.8-mile most-difficult loop beginning at the James A. Kell Visitor Center parking lot.
cards.access_notes: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; this route is rated most difficult, so choose it only if the group is prepared.

cards.title: Stroll Strawcutter Trail
cards.subtitle: Keystone State Park, near Latrobe
cards.notes: Walk the easier two-mile Strawcutter loop and use the wetland, meadow, and pine sections as natural conversation stops.
cards.short_summary: An easy loop crossing meadow, wetland, and pine-forest settings.
cards.evidence_claim: Strawcutter Trail is a 2.0-mile easiest-rated loop at Keystone State Park that passes a wetland, meadow, and pine forest.
cards.access_notes: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; remain on the designated trail.

cards.title: Watch for Migrating Birds
cards.subtitle: Keystone State Park, near Latrobe
cards.notes: Bring binoculars if you have them, scan quietly from established areas, and observe wildlife without approaching or handling any animals.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal bird-and-wildlife observation outing around Keystone’s lake and habitats.
cards.evidence_claim: Keystone State Park reports that warblers, kinglets, buffleheads, mergansers, herons, osprey, and other birds migrate through the park.
cards.source_title: Wildlife Watching at Keystone State Park
cards.access_notes: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; observe animals from a distance and do not handle them.

cards.title: Day Hike the Laurel Highlands Trail
cards.subtitle: Laurel Ridge State Park
cards.notes: Pick a daylight section from a designated trailhead, share the route with the group, and use the voluntary day-use registration mailbox.
cards.short_summary: A choose-your-distance day hike on Laurel Ridge’s long-distance trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Laurel Ridge State Park’s main feature is the 70-mile Laurel Highlands Hiking Trail; day hikers are asked to use voluntary registration mailboxes at trailheads.
cards.source_title: Stay the Night at Laurel Ridge State Park
cards.access_notes: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee. This card is for day hiking only; overnight use requires a reservation and fee.

cards.title: See Adams Falls
cards.subtitle: Linn Run State Park
cards.notes: Walk the one-mile loop with friends, stay on the designated route near the waterfall, and leave time to return before dusk.
cards.short_summary: A short state-park waterfall walk through rhododendron and hemlock.
cards.evidence_claim: DCNR describes Adams Falls Trail at Linn Run State Park as a one-mile loop leading to a mountain waterfall among rhododendron and hemlock.
cards.access_notes: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; use care around water and remain on the marked trail.

cards.title: Visit the Wetland Boardwalk
cards.subtitle: Winnie Palmer Nature Reserve, Saint Vincent College
cards.notes: Meet at the reserve and take a slow boardwalk lap to look for marsh birds and native plants; respect the habitat and posted rules.
cards.short_summary: A campus-adjacent marsh boardwalk for a low-key nature walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Winnie Palmer Nature Reserve identifies its Wetland Boardwalk as a place to see native marshes, red-winged blackbirds, cattails, and jewelweed.
cards.access_notes: The reserve lists trail hours as daily dawn to dusk and does not list an admission charge for visiting its trails.
